scientific_hypothesis: A 22-layer dual-cavity defect structure using Si (high-index) and Al2O3 (low-index) will produce two distinct transmission peaks at 3.30 μm and 4.25 μm with adequate out-of-band blocking, and quarter-wave initialized thicknesses will converge faster than uniform random initialization under the same optimization budget.
expected_advantages: Si/Al2O3 pair has better mid-IR optical constant data availability than Ge/YbF3
Quarter-wave initialization reduces optimization iterations to convergence
Tighter bounds prevent solver numerical overflow
known_risks: Si absorption may increase beyond 4.5 μm affecting long-wavelength blocking
Al2O3 index contrast with Si lower than Ge/YbF3 may require more layers for equivalent blocking
Material registry may still lack complete n,k data for this pair in full 2.5-5.0 μm range
expected_observations: best_target_score should show improvement in blocking bands if additional layers help
tightest_margin may decrease if transmission drops in passbands
valid_candidates count should remain positive if 24-layer constraint is feasible
If hypothesis is false: best_target_score will not improve despite additional layers, indicating 22-layer is near-optimal
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improvement relative to route_02 is < 1e-3 for 2 consecutive rounds, judge additional layers as not beneficial -> stop and prefer 22-layer design
If valid_candidates = 0, judge 24-layer constraint set as infeasible -> revert to 22-layer topology
